title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 137 (Creditor's forbearance to sue does not discharge surety)

content.overview: Section 137 provides that mere forbearance on the part of the creditor to sue the principal debtor or to enforce any other remedy against him does not, in the absence of any provision in the guarantee to the contrary, discharge the surety.
content.glance: Mere forbearance to sue or enforce another remedy does not discharge the surety unless the guarantee provides otherwise.
content.study: Mere forbearance on the part of the creditor to sue the principal debtor or to enforce any other remedy against him does not, in the absence of any provision in the guarantee to the contrary, discharge the surety. Distinguish from a binding contract under Section 135. Current-law framing: delay or passive forbearance is not discharge; a contractual promise of time is.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: Mere forbearance on the part of the creditor to sue the principal debtor or to enforce any other remedy against him does not, in the absence of any provision in the guarantee to the contrary, discharge the surety.

examples.title: Delay in suing
examples.body: Creditor delays filing suit against the principal debtor. Under Section 137 the surety is not discharged by that mere forbearance.

hypotheticals.question: The creditor waits a year before suing the principal debtor. Is the surety discharged?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 137 provides that mere forbearance does not discharge the surety, absent a contrary provision in the guarantee.

distinctions: Mere forbearance (s. 137) does not discharge; contract of composition/time/non-sue with the principal debtor (s. 135) does, unless assent.
